message.content:
**Short answer:** Yes – you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta. The city’s police department and the City of Atlanta’s 311 system are the primary ways to report it. If you want to involve your city council member, you can do that as well, but the first step is usually to contact the police or the city’s online portal. --- ## How to File a Noise Complaint in Atlanta | Step | What to Do | Where to Go / Who to Call | |------|------------|---------------------------| | **1. Identify the type of noise** | • Residential or commercial
• Daytime (8 am–10 pm) vs. nighttime (10 pm–8 am)
• Persistent vs. one‑off | • Helps the police determine priority | | **2. Call the Atlanta Police Department (APD)** | • Non‑emergency line: **404‑656‑3111** (or 311 from any phone in Atlanta)
• If you’re in an emergency (e.g., violent disturbance), call 911 | • APD will dispatch a unit if the noise violates the city’s noise ordinance | | **3. Use the City of Atlanta’s 311 Online Portal** | • Visit or use the 311 mobile app
• Select “Noise” under “Report a Problem” | • You’ll receive a ticket number and can track the status | | **4. Submit a Written Complaint (optional)** | • Fill out the online form or email: **noise@atlantaga.gov**
• Include:
 • Your name & contact info
 • Address of the noise source
 • Description of the noise (time, duration, type)
 • Any evidence (audio clip, photos) | • Useful if you want a formal record | | **5. Contact Your City Council Member** | • If the noise is a recurring problem or you’re not getting a response, reach out to the council member representing your district.
• Find your council member here: | • They can advocate on your behalf or refer you to the appropriate city department | --- ## Quick Reference | Resource | Link | What It Offers | |----------|------|----------------| | **Atlanta Police Department – Noise Ordinance** | | Full text of the ordinance, enforcement guidelines | | **City of Atlanta 311** | | Online reporting, status tracking | | **Noise Complaint Email** | **noise@atlantaga.gov** | Direct email for written complaints | | **City Council Contact** | | Find your council member’s office | | **Atlanta Police Non‑Emergency Line** | **404‑656‑3111** | Phone reporting | --- ## Things to Keep in Mind 1. **Noise Ordinance Hours** - *Daytime*: 8 am–10 pm – “normal” noise is allowed. - *Nighttime*: 10 pm–8 am – stricter limits; loud music, construction, or other disturbances are typically prohibited. 2. **Evidence Helps** - If possible, record a short audio clip or take a photo of the source (e.g., a construction site). - This can speed up the investigation. 3. **Follow‑Up** - After filing, you’ll receive a ticket number. Use it to check status on the 311 portal. - If the issue persists, you can file a follow‑up complaint or ask your council member for assistance. 4. **When to Call 911** - If the noise is accompanied by a threat of violence, a disturbance that could lead to injury, or if you feel unsafe, call 911 immediately. --- ### Bottom Line Yes, you can report a noise complaint in Atlanta. Start with the Atlanta Police Department’s non‑emergency line or the city’s 311 portal, and if you need additional support, contact your local city council member. The city’s noise ordinance is enforced by the police, so they’ll be the ones to investigate and take action.
